ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p6/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p6/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p6/r2.claim: The Prophet's assumed burden of preaching exceeds what is required of him; the verse begins to clarify his limited responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p6/r2.anchor: the burden he is bearing as a result is not required of him at all.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r1.claim: The Prophet's duty is to communicate the Book; he need not force it on people unable to recognize truth and fear God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r1.anchor: is to communicate this Book to people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p7/r2.claim: Seeing persistent denial and hard hearts made the Prophet worry that his effort was inadequate, but the verse reassures him not to exceed his duty or feel responsible for others' acceptance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p308/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p308/r5.speaker: علي والضحاك ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p308/r5.claim: ʿAlī links revelation to the Prophet alternating his weight while standing; al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil report Quraysh’s claims that the Quran made him suffer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p308/r5.anchor: كان عليه السلام يراوح بين قدميه يقوم على رجل فنزلت قاله علي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r6.speaker: طلحة والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r6.claim: Ṭalḥa reads mā nuzzila in the passive with al-Qurʾān nominative; the majority reads mā anzalnā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r6.anchor: وقرأ طلحة ما نزل عليك بنون مضمومة وزاي مكسورة مشددة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r7.claim: Litashqā means suffering from grief over unbelief; al-Zamakhsharī says the Messenger need only convey and remind, not guarantee belief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r7.anchor: ومعنى لتشقى لتتعب بفرط تأسفك عليهم وعلى كفرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r8.claim: Another explanation takes the verse as a reply to Abū Jahl and others; the lām marks the shift from God as sender to the Messenger as addressee.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p309/r8.anchor: وقيل: أريد رد ما قاله أبو جهل وغيره مما تقدم ذكره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows an tashqā without the preposition, accusative after dropping it, by analogy with another Quranic construction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r1.anchor: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن أن تشقى كقوله أن تحبط أعمالكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r2.claim: Case after dropping a preposition is disputed: the verb may govern the accusative, or the omitted preposition may remain operative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p310/r2.anchor: وليس كون أن تشقى إذا حذف الجار منصوبا متفقا عليه بل في ذلك خلاف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr explains that after Mary names blessed prophets and warns of corrupt successors, the prospect might alarm Muhammad, so the next surah reassures him that the Qur'an was not sent to make him miserable.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12/r3.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير في بر هانه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r1.claim: Maryam closes by recalling destroyed generations after warning a stubborn people; seeing Quraysh resist made the Prophet grieve, and God reassures him that revelation was not sent to burden him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r1.anchor: وأيضا فقد ختمت سورة مريم يقوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r2.claim: The Prophet's grief reflected fear that Quraysh would not respond and his labor would be prolonged; receptive people who fear God will respond when reminded and shown God's signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r2.anchor: فيطول العناء والمشقة , فبشره سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r3.claim: The reassurance parallels the command not to let their words grieve him, then is followed by mention of the All-Merciful established over the Throne.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p12#2/r3.anchor: كما قيل له في موضع آخر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p8/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8/r3.claim: The surah honors the Prophet by assuring him that gentle patience will draw hearts and grow his community; God calmed and protected early Muslims, softened Umar into a defender, and prevents their annihilation like the peoples of Noah and Hud.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8/r3.anchor: تشريف هذا النبي الكريم صلى الله عليه وسلم بإعلامه بالرفق بأمته

BIQAI-FULL:v5p8/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8/r4.claim: Because Maryam ends with the destruction of earlier nations while Muhammad had few believers, this surah reassures him that his people will not be wiped out by punishment as those nations were.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8/r4.anchor: لما ختم تلك بإهلاك القرون وإبادة الأمم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r1.claim: The denial that the Qur'an was sent to make the Prophet suffer addresses his fear that few would follow him after his people were destroyed; instead it is a reminder for those who fear God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p8#2/r1.anchor: أي بتعب قلبك بكونك من أقل المرسلين تابعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r2.claim: One interpretation of la-tashqā is that the Prophet was exhausting himself in worship and standing in prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r2.anchor: لتبلغ من نفسك في العبادة والقيام في الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r3.claim: Quraysh saw the Prophet’s austere life and abundant worship and said Muhammad was suffering with his Lord; the revelation answered them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r3.anchor: إنما سبب الآية أن قريش لما نظرت إلى عيش رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وشظفه وكثرة عبادته قالت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r4.claim: The Quraysh-context reading is broader in the scope of misery: the apparent hardship is the soul’s bliss, and God sent the Qurʾān for lasting felicity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p37/r4.anchor: فهذا التأويل أعم من الأول في لفظة الشقاء

MAJAZ:v2p15/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p15/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p15/r1.claim: Ṭā Hā functions like the disconnected letters opening other sūrahs, with the same introductory function.
MAJAZ:v2p15/r1.anchor: ساكن لأنه جرى مجرى فواتح سائر السور اللواتى مجازهن مجاز حروف التهجي ومجاز موضعه فى المعنى كمجاز ابتداء فواتح سائر السور

MAJAZ:v2p15/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p15/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p15/r2.claim: Abū Ṭufayla al-Ḥaramazī claims that Ṭā Hā means “O man.”

MAJAZ:v2p15/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p15/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p15/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda rejects treating Ṭā Hā as a name because it is indeclinable in this explanation; a name would take case inflection.
MAJAZ:v2p15/r3.anchor: ولا ينبغى أن يكون اسما لأنه ساكن ولو كان اسما لدخله الإعراب.

JISHUMI:v6p4628/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r8.claim: Shaqāwa is the opposite of happiness and denotes hardship that continues to burden the soul.
JISHUMI:v6p4628/r8.anchor: والشقاوة: استمرار ما يشق على النفس.

JISHUMI:v6p4636/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4636/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4636/r5.claim: Whoever adheres to the Quran will never suffer; some explain the promised relief as abrogating night prayer, while al-Hasan and Abu Ali take it as relief from afterlife hardship and thus general.
JISHUMI:v6p4636/r5.anchor: من تمسك بالقرآن لا يشقى أبدا

NAHHAS:v3p31/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p31/r8.speaker: بعض النحويين
NAHHAS:v3p31/r8.claim: Some grammarians call the lām one of negation, while others call it the lām of denial.
NAHHAS:v3p31/r8.anchor: بعض النحويين يقول هذه لام النفي وبعضهم يقول لام الجحود

NAHHAS:v3p31/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p31/r9.speaker: ابن كيسان
NAHHAS:v3p31/r9.claim: Ibn Kaysan calls it the lām of lowering and interprets the verse as “We did not send the Qur’an to make you miserable.”
NAHHAS:v3p31/r9.anchor: وسمعت أبا الحسن بن كيسان يقول في مثلها إنها لام الخفض والمعنى عنده ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن للشقاء

NAHHAS:v3p31/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p31/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p31/r10.claim: Shaqāʾ may be lengthened or shortened, and derives from a root with wāw.
NAHHAS:v3p31/r10.anchor: والشقاء يمد ويقصر وهو من ذوات الواو

RAZI-FULL:v22p5#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p5#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p5#2/r1.claim: By attributing revelation to the Creator of earth and lofty heavens, God magnifies the Qur'an to encourage reflection on its meanings; honoring the sender's message invites obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v22p5#2/r1.anchor: تعظيم الله تعالى يظهر بتعظيم خلقه ونعمه وإنما عظم القرآن ترغيبا في تدبره والتأمل في معانيه وحقائقه

TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet lifted one leg during prayer to increase his exertion, prompting the opening reassurance that the Qur'an was not sent to make him suffer.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r3.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يرفع إحدى رجليه في الصلاة ليزيد تعبه

TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r4.claim: The same account of the Prophet lifting a leg in prayer until revelation came is also attributed to Abu Abd Allah.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r4.anchor: وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r5.speaker: أبو بصير عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r5.claim: The Imams report that the Prophet prayed on his toes until they swelled; the revelation begins with “Taha,” glossed as “O Muhammad” in Tayy speech.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r5.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام قالا كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إذا صلى قام على أصابع رجليه حتى تورم

TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r6.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r6.claim: A report from Ali says that after the command to pray at night the Prophet stood all night until his feet swelled, alternating his feet; Gabriel then said “Taha,” meaning earth with your feet, and the reassurance followed.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r6.anchor: عن علي قال لما نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم { يا أيها المزمل قم الليل إلا قليلا } قام الليل كله حتى تورمت قدماه

TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r7.claim: The author considers the Ali account the likely original story, with other reports selecting different details of the same swollen-foot prayer as the occasion of revelation.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r7.anchor: والمظنون المطابق للاعتبار أن تكون هذه الرواية هي الأصل في القصة

TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r8.claim: The narrative's fit with the surrounding verses, taken in their context, is unclear.
TABATABAI:20:1-8#3/r8.anchor: أن في انطباق الآيات بما لها من السياق على القصة خفاء

TABRISI:20:2-8/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r2.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:20:2-8/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verse answers polytheists who called the Prophet wretched: the Qurʾān was sent to prepare and honor him in this life and the next.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن هو جواب للمشركين حين قالوا إنه شقي

TABRISI:20:2-8/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:2-8/r3.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:20:2-8/r3.claim: Qatādah says the Prophet prayed the whole night and tied his chest with a rope to keep sleep away, so God ordered him to ease his burden.
TABRISI:20:2-8/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: وكان يصلي الليل كله ويعلق صدره بحبل

THALABI:v6p237/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p237/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p237/r6.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet and companions tied ropes across their chests for night prayer, thinking it obligatory, and the verse was revealed.
THALABI:v6p237/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه يربطون الحبال في صدورهم في الصلاة بالليل ذلك بالفرض، وأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية.

THALABI:v6p237/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p237/r7.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p237/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi says revelation in Mecca led the Prophet to intensify worship and pray all night; after this verse he slept as well as praying.
THALABI:v6p237/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لما نزل على رسول الله الوحي بمكة اجتهد في العبادة واشتدت عبادته فجعل يصلي الليل كله

THALABI:v6p237/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p237/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v6p237/r8.claim: Mughira ibn Shuʿba reports that the Prophet prayed until his feet swelled and replied that he should be a grateful servant when asked why, given his forgiveness.
THALABI:v6p237/r8.anchor: سمعت المغيرة بن شعبة يقول: قام رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى تورمت قدماه، وقيل له: يا رسول الله أليس قد غفر الله لك

THALABI:v6p237/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p237/r9.speaker: أبو جهل بن هشام والنصر بن الحرث
THALABI:v6p237/r9.claim: Muqatil says Abu Jahl and al-Nadr criticized the Prophet's strenuous worship, alleging he was wretched; the verse answered them that the Qur'an was sent as admonition to the fearful.
THALABI:v6p237/r9.anchor: قال مقاتل: قال أبو جهل بن هشام والنصر بن الحرث للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنك لتسعى بترك ديننا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:3-5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:3-5/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:3-5/r2.claim: The Quran was not sent to make the Prophet toil from excessive effort; he prayed all night in Mecca until his feet swelled, and disbelievers said he suffered by leaving their religion, so this verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:3-5/r2.anchor: لتتعب بكثرة الجهد، وذلك أنه كان يصلي الليل كله بمكة حتى تورمت قدماه، وقال له الكفار: إنك لتشقى بترك ديننا

SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r1.speaker: طلحة
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r1.claim: The common reading is أنزلنا; Talha reads ما نزل in the passive, with القرآن raised as نائب الفاعل.
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r1.anchor: هذه قراءة العامة. وقرأ طلحة " ما نزل " مبنيا للمفعول، " القرآن " رفع لقيامه مقام فاعله

SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r2.claim: If Ṭā Hā is the names of the letters, the clause may stand independently.
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r2.anchor: وهذه الجملة يجوز أن تكون مستأنفة إن جعلت " طه " تعديدا لأسماء الحروف

SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r3.claim: If Ṭā Hā names the sūrah, the clause may be its predicate; القرآن then appears in place of a pronoun because Ṭā Hā is itself Qur'an.
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r3.anchor: خبرا ل طه إن جعلتها اسما للسورة ويكون القرآن ظاهرا واقعا موقع المضمر؛ لأن طه قرآن أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r4.claim: If Ṭā Hā is an object of oath, the clause may be the oath's answer; the fuller discussion is earlier in the work.
SAMIN-DURR:20:2/r4.anchor: جواب قسم، إن جعلت طه مقسما به

SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows ما أنزلنا أن تشقى, by analogy with 49:2, but treats its accusative as secondary after dropping a preposition, unlike the basic object تذكرة.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3/r2.anchor: هذا كلام الزمخشري، ثم قال: " فإن قلت: " هل يجوز أن تقول: ما أنزلنا

SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa rejects making لتشقى govern تذكرة as semantically unsound; al-Zamakhshari explains that toil can be the route to a reminder.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r3.anchor: إلا أن أبا البقاء لما لم يظهر له هذا المعنى الذي ظهر للزمخشري منع من عمل " لتشقى " في " تذكرة "

SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari justifies calling the burden شقاء because the word can mean toil, citing the proverbs about a colt trainer.
SAMIN-DURR:20:3#2/r4.anchor: والشقاء يجيء في معنى التعب. ومنه المثل: " أتعب من رائض مهر " و " أشقى من رائض مهر

ZAJJAJ:v3p349/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p349/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p349/r4.claim: The Qur'an was not sent down to make the Prophet strain by praying on one leg.
ZAJJAJ:v3p349/r4.anchor: أي لتصلي على إحدى رجليك فتشتد عليك،

ASAD-NOTES:20:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:1#n2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:1#n2/r1.claim: Qur'anic ethical discipline does not constrict life; it deepens awareness of right and wrong and thereby enhances life.
ASAD-NOTES:20:1#n2/r1.anchor: the ethical discipline imposed upon man by the teachings of the Qur'an is not meant to narrow down his feel of life, but, on the contrary, to enhance it

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r1.claim: The disjoint letters occur beyond the Ḥā Mīm sūras and usually lead into discussion of the Qur'an; the best known view is that Arabs are challenged to match revelation made from their own speech elements.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r1.anchor: وأشهر ما قيل في ذلك أن هذا الكتاب الذي تحداكم به وأنزله رب العالمين هو من مفردات كلامكم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r2.claim: Another reported view is that the disjoint letters are combined to form words.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1084/r2.anchor: وقسم قال أنه يجمع بين الأحرف

QIRAAT-ER:20:2:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:2:4#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:20:2:4#1/r1.claim: The hamza-less qurān form simplifies pronunciation; the source says it carries no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:20:2:4#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Hamza simplification — drops the hamza (ʾ) yielding qurān instead of qurʾān; this is a phonological variant

ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r1.claim: The verse is an independent consolation for the Prophet over the strain caused by the opponents: the Qur'an was not sent to burden him in dispute with obstinate leaders or in grief at their rejection, but to convey and remind; compare 18:6.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r1.anchor: عما كان يعتريه من جهد المشركين من التعب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r2.claim: Here شقاء means toil and distress, illustrated by the proverb about a colt trainer and a poem contrasting the rational person who suffers with the ignorant person who enjoys hardship.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r2.anchor: الشقاء شاسع في ذلك المعنى ومنه المثل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r3.claim: The Prophet was not sent to exhaust himself through debate and excessive sorrow for their disbelief; he has delivered and reminded, so their refusal after that is no fault of his.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r3.anchor: بل لتبلغ وتذكر وقد فعلت فلا عليك أن لم يؤمنوا بعد ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r4.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r4.claim: A report from Ali cited through Ibn Mardawayh is used for the alternative that the verse turns the Prophet away from excessive exertion in worship and harsh ascetic disciplines; he was sent with the tolerant, upright religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r4.anchor: كما سمعت فيما أخرج ابن مردويه عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجه أي ما أنزلناه عليك لتتعب بنهك نفسك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r5.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r5.claim: Muqatil reports that Abu Jahl, al-Naḍr ibn al-Harith, and al-Muṭʿim told the Prophet, after seeing his worship, that abandoning their religion and receiving the Qur'an made him suffer; God denied their claim.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r5.anchor: أن أبا جهل والنظر بن الحرث والمطعم قالوا لرسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r6.claim: The opponents may use شقاء literally as the opposite of happiness, while God's use echoes their wording by rhetorical matching.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r6.anchor: والشقاء في كلامهم يحتمل أن يكون بمعناه الحقيقي وهو ضد السعادة والتعبير به في كلامه تعالى من باب المشاكله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r7.claim: If Ṭā Hā denotes the Qur'an, it may be nominative as the subject of the following sentence; repeating القرآن instead of a linking pronoun signals that the Qur'an is comforting mercy, not a cause of suffering.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r7.anchor: فيجوز فيه أن يكون محله الرفع على الأبتداء والجملة بعده خبره وقد أقيم فيها الظاهر أعنى القرآن مقام الضمير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r8.claim: Other parses make the following clause predicate-less or the predicate of an omitted subject, treat Ṭā Hā as an object after an implied recite, or take it as an oath with its particle omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p149#2/r8.anchor: هو خبر لمبتدأ محذوف والجملة على القولين مستانفة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r1.claim: If Ṭā Hā is the Qur'an specifically meaning this sura, the following sentence can refer back to it; a general Qur'an reading also links through its inclusion of the sura.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r1.anchor: فالربط به لشموله للمبتدأ كما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r3.claim: Some reject making the sura the subject when the next sentence is its predicate: denial of suffering presupposes earlier toil, which could not have resulted from revelation of this newly revealed sura; Alusi finds this objection reasonable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r3.anchor: لأن نفي كون انزال القرآن للشقاء يستدعي وقوع الشقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r8.speaker: طلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p150/r8.claim: Talha reads ما نزل عليك القرآن with a doubled zāy and passive voice, making القرآن the subject of the verb.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r6.claim: One esoteric reading says the reminder recalls the days of union before souls entered bodies and promises their return; alternatively, it reminds them of those days to stir longing, tears, and effort toward regaining them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p208/r6.anchor: أي إلا لتذكر من يخشى ايام الوصال التى كانت قبل تعلق الأرواح بالابدان وتخبرهم بانها يحصل نحوها لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r11.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r11.claim: Al-Kalbī says the Prophet prayed all night and shifted weight between his feet during long standing; this verse told him to ease his effort.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r11.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لما نزل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي بمكة اجتهد في العبادة حتى كان يراوح بين قدميه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r12.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r12.claim: Another occasion says the polytheists saw his strenuous worship and claimed the Qur'an was sent to make him suffer; the verse answered them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: لما رأى المشركون اجتهاده في العبادة قالوا ما أنزل عليك القرآن يا محمد إلا لشقائك، فنزلت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r13.claim: Shiqā means to toil and become tired; toil is its basic linguistic sense.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p259#2/r13.anchor: أي لتتعنى وتتعب، وأصل الشقاء في اللغة العناء

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r1.claim: Depending on how Ṭā Hā is parsed, the clause can be its predicate, an oath’s answer, its vocative answer, or a resumption; Qur’an may resume Ṭā Hā as antecedent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r1.anchor: خبر { طه } إن جعلته مبتدأ على أنه مؤول بالسورة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r2.claim: God did not send the Qur’an to make the Prophet suffer through excessive grief at Quraysh’s disbelief, since his duty is only to convey.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r2.anchor: والمعنى: ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتتعب بفرط تأسفك على كفر قريش إذ ما عليك إلا أن تبلغ

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the verse does not burden him with excessive spiritual discipline, long night vigils, and standing for worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r3.anchor: أو بكثرة الرياضة وكثرة التهجد والقيام على ساق

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r4.claim: Shaqāʾ commonly means toil, as in the proverb about a horse trainer and a chief being most burdened; the wording implies the Qur’an was sent to make him blessed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r4.anchor: والشقاء شائع بمعنى التعب ومنه أشقى من رائض المهر، وسيد القوم أشقاهم. ولعله عدل إليه للإشعار بأنه أنزل عليه ليسعد.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r5.claim: Another view says the verse rebuts unbelievers who saw his worship and claimed he suffered by leaving their religion and receiving the Qur’an.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:2/r5.anchor: وقيل رد وتكذيب للكفرة، فإنهم لما رأوا كثرة عبادته قالوا إنك لتشقى بترك ديننا

DURR-FULL:v5p548/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that at the beginning of revelation the Prophet stood on the balls of his feet while praying, and then this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أول ما أنزل عليه الوحي كان يقوم على صدور قدميه

DURR-FULL:v5p548/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says people remarked that this man had made himself wretched for his Lord, prompting the revelation of the verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قالوا لقد شقي هذا الرجل بربه فأنزل الله: {طه ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى}

DURR-FULL:v5p548/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet tied himself with a rope during night worship so that he would not fall asleep, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قام من الليل يربط نفسه بحبل كي لا ينام

DURR-FULL:v5p548/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r11.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet tied himself and placed one leg over the other before this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p548/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يربط نفسه ويضع إحدى رجليه على الأخرى فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v5p549/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r1.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r1.claim: Ali reports that after the command to keep night vigil the Prophet prayed all night until his feet swelled; Gabriel told him to put his feet on the ground, and this verse and the easing command in 73:20 followed.
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r1.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: لما نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم (يا أيها المزمل قم الليل إلا قليلا)

DURR-FULL:v5p549/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r2.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r2.claim: In a report Bazzar grades hasan, Ali says the Prophet shifted his weight between his feet until this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r2.anchor: عن علي قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يراوح بين قدميه يقوم على كل رجل حتى نزلت

DURR-FULL:v5p549/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r3.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r3.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says the Prophet used to pray standing on one foot; Ṭā Hā means ‘tread the earth,’ and the verse relieved this hardship.
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r3.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى قام على رجل ورفع الأخرى فأنزل الله {طه} يعني طأ الأرض يا محمد

DURR-FULL:v5p549/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet sometimes prayed reciting Qur’an while standing on one foot; Ṭā Hā instructed him to stand on both feet.
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r4.anchor: عن بان عباس في قوله: {طه} قال: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ربما قرأ القرآن إذا صلى قام على رجل واحدة فأنزل الله {طه} برجليك

DURR-FULL:v5p549/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r5.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak says Quraysh disbelievers claimed God sent the Qur’an only to make Muhammad suffer, and the verse answered them.
DURR-FULL:v5p549/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: لما أنزل الله القرآن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قام به وأصحابه فقال له كفار قريش

DURR-FULL:v5p551/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r1.claim: Mujahid says ‘not to make you suffer’ concerns prayer and parallels the command to recite what is easy in 73:20; people used to tie ropes to their chests while praying.
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى} يقول: في الصلاة هي مثل قوله

DURR-FULL:v5p551/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r2.claim: Qatada insists God did not make Muhammad wretched: the Qur’an is mercy, light, and a guide to Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p551/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى} يا رجل

BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r1.claim: Here shaqāʾ commonly means exertion, illustrated by the hard labor of a horse trainer who makes a foal rideable; the saying serves as a proverb.
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r1.anchor: الشقاء شائع بمعنى التعب ومن أشقى من رائض المهر

BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r2.claim: The Prophet was not sent to exhaust himself grieving over Quraysh’s unbelief: his duty was to convey, which he had done, and their later belief was not his responsibility.
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r2.anchor: لتتعب بفرط تأسك على كفر قريش إذ ما عليك إلا البلاغ وقد فعلت

BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r3.claim: The verse also rejects excessive ascetic exercise and night vigil: the Prophet was sent with a tolerant, upright religion, not to stand all night until his legs were injured.
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r3.anchor: أو بكثرة الرياضة وكثرة التهجد والقيام على ساق إذ ما بعثت إلا بالحنيفية السمحة

BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r4.claim: The Qur’an was revealed to make the Prophet happy through embodying its character, and to make the inhabitants of the heavens and earth happy through his noble character.
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r4.anchor: في الدنيا أو العقبى بل أنزلناه على قلبك لتسعد بتخلقك بخلقه

BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r5.speaker: أبو جهل والنضر بن الحارث
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r5.claim: Bursevī says Abū Jahl and al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith called the Prophet wretched for leaving his forefathers’ religion and claimed the Qur’an would make him miserable.
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r5.anchor: فإن أبا جهل والنضر بن الحارث قالا له : إنك شقي

BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r6.claim: Against their charge, Islam and the Qur’an lead to every success and happiness; the unbelievers’ condition is misery itself.
BURSEVI:v5p278#3/r6.anchor: بأن دين الإسلام وهذا القرآن هو السلم إلى نيل كل فوز والسبب في درك كل سعادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.claim: The ending closes the debate and echoes the opening: the Prophet has delivered guidance, so he may take comfort in completing his mission while the heedless remain astray until truth becomes clear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p349/r1.anchor: وهي قوله { ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى } ( طه : 2 )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#2/r1.claim: Toil means exhausting oneself through effort; the Prophet had striven so intensely in worship that he alternated his weight between his feet during long standing, so he was instructed to ease up.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p270#2/r1.anchor: لتتعب وتبلغ من الجهد ما قد بلغت وذلك أنه اجتهد في العبادة وبالغ حتى إنه كان يرواح بين قدميه لطول القيام فأمر بالتخفيف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p271#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p271#2/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p271#2/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ b. Anas reports that the Prophet prayed standing on one leg with the other raised; God revealed “Ṭā Hā”—“press the ground, Muḥammad”—and said He had not sent the Qurʾan to distress him. Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ calls this an unmistakable honor and kindness.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p271#2/r4.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى قام على رجل ورفع الأخرى، فأنزل الله تعالى {طه}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, through Juwaybir, says that when the Qurʾan was revealed the Prophet and Companions prayed with it; Quraysh claimed it had been sent only to make Muḥammad suffer, so 20:1–3 was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r1.anchor: قال جويبر، عن الضحاك: لما أنزل الله القرآن على رسوله، قام به هو وأصحابه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r2.claim: Against the false claim, knowledge from God is great good; the Prophet says God grants understanding of religion to whomever He wishes good, reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r2.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيحين، عن معاوية قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī transmits a report from Thalabah b. al-Ḥakam: on Judgment Day God tells scholars He gave them knowledge and wisdom intending to forgive them; Ibn Kathīr grades its chain good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r3.anchor: عن ثعلبة بن الحكم قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r4.claim: Thalabah is identified as al-Laythī; Abū ʿUmar notes he settled in Basra, later moved to Kufa, and Samāk b. Ḥarb narrated from him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r4.anchor: ذكره أبو عمر في استيعابه، وقال: نزل البصرة، ثم تحول إلى الكوفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r5.claim: Mujāhid likens the verse to 73:20 and says the Companions used to tie ropes to their chests while praying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد في قوله: {ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى} : هي كقوله:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r6.claim: Qatādah says God did not make the Qurʾan hardship; He made it mercy, light, and a guide to Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p272/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: {ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى} : لا والله ما جعله شقاء، ولكن جعله رحمة ونورا

JISHUMI:v6p4633/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r5.claim: One explanation says the Quran was not sent to make Muḥammad tired or miserable in this life; another says it brings happiness in the afterlife through conveying and practicing it.
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r5.anchor: قيل: لتتعب، لتصير به شقيا في الدنيا، وقيل: ما أنزلناه لتشقى به في الآخرة؛ بل لتسعد به

JISHUMI:v6p4633/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r6.claim: Abū Muslim says the Prophet is not accountable for his people's deeds or blameworthy for them; his duty is only to convey.
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r6.anchor: أنك لا تؤخذ بفعل قومك ولا تلام وإنما عليك البلاغ، ونحو ذلك: (وما أرسلناك عليهم وكيلا).

JISHUMI:v6p4633/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r7.claim: Abū Muslim also says the Prophet should not grieve or exhaust himself over their rejection: the Quran is a reminder, belief benefits each person, and disbelief should not distress him.
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r7.anchor: لا تحزن عليهم ولا تعذب نفسك، فإنما أنزلنا القرآن تذكرة، فمن آمن فلنفسه ومن كفر فلا يحزنك كفره

JISHUMI:v6p4633/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r8.claim: The warning not to grieve for rejection is reinforced by the parallel address in 18:6.
JISHUMI:v6p4633/r8.anchor: نظيره (فلعلك باخع نفسك على آثارهم إن لم يؤمنوا بهذا الحديث أسفا (6).

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r10.claim: The Quran was not sent to make the Prophet toil and stay awake in night prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r10.anchor: بالتعب والسهر في قيام الليل , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r11.claim: The verse answers the polytheists, who claimed that the Quran had made the Prophet wretched.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r11.anchor: أنه جواب للمشركين لما قالوا : إنه بالقرآن شقى , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r12.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r12.claim: It means the Prophet should not grieve over his people's disbelief.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p392#2/r12.anchor: معناه لا تشق بالحزن والأسف على كفر قومك , قاله ابن بحر

MUJAHID:v1p393/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p393/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p393/r1.claim: The Prophet's hardship was in prayer; Mujahid compares it to the instruction to recite what is easy, noting that people tied ropes to their chests during prayer.
MUJAHID:v1p393/r1.anchor: ﴿ طه ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى ﴾ يعني في الصلاة وهو كقوله

MUQATIL:20:2-4/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:2-4/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:2-4/r2.claim: Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and al-Mutʿim ibn ʿAdi said the Prophet suffered for leaving his fathers' religion and called him wretched after he said he was sent as a mercy; the verse answered them.
MUQATIL:20:2-4/r2.anchor: إنك لتشقى حين تركت دين آبائك

MUQATIL:20:2-4/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:2-4/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:2-4/r3.claim: The Quran was sent as a reminder for whoever fears God, from the Creator of the earth and seven high heavens, not to make Muhammad suffer.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r1.claim: If Ṭā Hā enumerates disconnected letter names, this begins a new statement.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r1.anchor: ان جعلت طه تعديدا لاسماء الحروف فهو ابتداء كلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r2.claim: If Ṭā Hā names the sūra, the clause may predicate of it with the sūra as subject; al-Qurʾān appears overtly instead of a pronoun because the sūra is Qurʾān.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r2.anchor: احتملت أن تكون خبرا عنها وهي في موضع المبتدأ والقرآن ظاهرا وقع موقع المضمر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the statement is the response to an oath treating Ṭā Hā as its subject.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r3.anchor: وأن يكون جوابا لها وهي قسم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r4.claim: The Prophet is not to exhaust himself in grief over the unbelievers and their refusal to believe, or through night worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r4.anchor: لتتعب لفرط تأسفك عليهم وعلى كفرهم وتحسرك على ان يؤمنوا أو بقيام الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r5.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled, and Gabriel told him to spare himself because his soul had rights; revelation did not come to exhaust him, and his mission is the easy, upright religion.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p50#2/r5.anchor: وأنه روى أنه عليه السلام صلى بالليل حت تورمت قدماه فقال له جبريل ابق على نفسك فان لها عليك حقا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r1.claim: The excerpt cites two descriptions of terror cast into disbelievers’ hearts as parallels during its discussion of Ṭā-Hā; the preceding gloss is not preserved here.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r1.anchor: سنلقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب [آل عمران: 151] وقوله: وقذف في قلوبهم الرعب [الأحزاب: 26].

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r2.claim: One gloss assigns ṭāʾ to the joy of Paradise’s people and hāʾ to the humiliation of the people of Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r2.anchor: وقيل: الطاء طرب أهل الجنة في الجنة، والهاء هوان أهل النار في النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r3.speaker: مجاهد ومحمد بن الحنفية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r3.claim: A sixth gloss understands Ṭā-Hā as blessedness for whoever is guided.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r3.anchor: وقول سادس: إن معنى «طه» طوبى لمن اهتدى قاله مجاهد ومحمد بن الحنفية.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r4.claim: A seventh gloss takes Ṭā-Hā as an imperative to tread the ground: the Prophet’s strenuous prayer nearly swelled his feet and required him to rest them in turn.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r4.anchor: وقول سابع: إن معنى «طه» طإ الأرض وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتحمل من مشقة الصلاة حتى كادت قدماه تتورم، ويحتاج إلى الترويح بين قدميه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r5.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r5.claim: Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ cites al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas: the Prophet prayed standing on one foot with the other raised, so Ṭā-Hā told him to plant both feet on the ground.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر القاضي عياض في «الشفاء» أن الربيع بن أنس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى قام على رجل ورفع الأخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r6.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reports al-Ḥasan’s interpretation of Ṭā-Hā as an order to tread with both feet, since the Prophet stood on one foot in night prayer; the original طأ was altered to ṭāʾ-hāʾ, with hāʾ of pause.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r6.anchor: الزمخشري: وعن الحسن «طه» وفسر بأنه أمر بالوطء، وأن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام كان يقوم في تهجده على إحدى رجليه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r7.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet and his companions tied ropes around their chests during lengthy night prayers; this practice was superseded by the obligation, and the verse was revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه يربطون الحبال في صدورهم في الصلاة بالليل من طول القيام، ثم نسخ ذلك بالفرض

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī says the Prophet’s intense worship after the Meccan revelation led him to pray all night; this verse instructed him to ease himself by praying and sleeping, ending the all-night standing practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r8.anchor: وقال الكلبي: لما نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي بمكة اجتهد في العبادة، واشتدت عبادته، فجعل يصلي الليل كله زمانا حتى نزلت هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r9.speaker: مقاتل والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r9.claim: Muqātil and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say Quraysh claimed the Qurʾān had been sent only to make Muhammad suffer after he and his companions prayed; God answered that it was not sent to distress him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل والضحاك: فلما نزل القرآن على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قام هو وأصحابه فصلوا، فقال كفار قريش: ما أنزل الله هذا القرآن على محمد إلا ليشقى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r10.claim: On this gloss, Ṭā-Hā is طاها, an imperative to tread the ground with both feet during prayer; hāʾ and alif refer to the ground, and hamza is lightened to a silent alif.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا القول: إن «طه» طاها أي طإ الأرض فتكون الهاء والألف ضمير الأرض، أي طإ الأرض برجليك في صلواتك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r11.speaker: طائفة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r11.claim: A group reads Ṭā-Hā as deriving from طأ, meaning tread the ground, with hamza dropped and hāʾ of pause added.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r11.anchor: وقرأت طائفة «طه» وأصله طأ بمعنى طإ الأرض فحذفت الهمزة وأدخلت هاء السكت.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r12.speaker: زر بن حبيش
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r12.claim: Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh reports that when a man argued that the Prophet had been told to tread the ground, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd answered Ṭā-Hā was exactly how the Messenger taught him to recite it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r12.anchor: وقال زر بن حبيش: قرأ رجل على عبد الله بن مسعود { طه * ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى } فقال له عبد الله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r13.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Abū Isḥāq incline hāʾ and open ṭāʾ; Abū Bakr, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and al-Aʿmash incline both; Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, and Nāfiʿ use an intermediate sound, chosen by Abū ʿUbayd; the rest use full emphasis.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r13.anchor: وأمال أبو عمرو وأبو إسحاق الهاء وفتحا الطاء. وأمالهما جميعا أبو بكر وحمزة والكسائي والأعمش.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r14.speaker: الثعلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r14.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī considers all these pronunciations correct, eloquent dialect forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r14.anchor: قال الثعلبي: وهي كلها لغات صحيحة فصيحة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r15.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r15.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects imāla as lacking a yāʾ or kasra to motivate it and because ṭāʾ is among the letters that block it.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r15.anchor: النحاس: لا وجه للإمالة عند أكثر أهل العربية لعلتين: إحداهما أنه ليس ها هنا ياء ولا كسرة فتكون الإمالة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r16.claim: A variant reading has ما نزل عليك القرآن لتشقى.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:2/r16.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى } وقرىء «ما نزل عليك القرآن لتشقى».

QASHANI:20:2-4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:2-4/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:2-4/r2.claim: Out of mercy and love for his people, the Prophet grieved that revelation did not move them to faith and feared a personal shortcoming.
QASHANI:20:2-4/r2.anchor: من شدة حنوه وتعطفه على قومه لكونه صورة الرحمة ومظهر المحبة، تأسف

QASHANI:20:2-4/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:2-4/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:2-4/r3.claim: Their disbelief stems from their side: hardened veils and absent receptivity, not the Prophet's ego, residual selfhood, or failure to guide.
QASHANI:20:2-4/r3.anchor: أخبر أن عدم إيمانهم ليس من جهتك بل من جهتهم وغلظ حجابهم أعدم استعدادهم

QASHANI:20:2-4/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:2-4/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:2-4/r4.claim: The names Pure and Guide free the Prophet from imputations of residual selfhood or deficient guidance; the Quran is a reminder for receptive, softened hearts after his purification.
QASHANI:20:2-4/r4.anchor: نودي باسمين من أسماء الله تعالى دالين على نزاهته عن الأمرين المذكورين

QASHANI:20:2-4/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:2-4/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:2-4/r5.claim: Spiritual discipline has already produced in the Prophet the two qualities signified by those names, making him perfected and perfecting; hard hearts explain why his guidance has no effect.
QASHANI:20:2-4/r5.anchor: ما المقصود بالرياضة إلا هذان الأمران اللذان ظهرا فيك تجلينا عليك بالاسمين المذكورين

QASHANI:20:2-4/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:2-4/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:2-4/r6.claim: Alternatively, the opening is an oath by the two names disclosed to him for purification and spiritual refinement, not a direct address; revelation's aim is their effect in him, not toil.
QASHANI:20:2-4/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون قسما لا نداء، أي: أقسم بالاسمين

RAZI-FULL:v22p4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4/r6.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p4/r6.claim: If Ṭā Hā counts as letter names, the verse begins a new sentence; if it names the sūra, the following clause may predicate of it, with القرآن replacing its pronoun, or answer an oath.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4/r6.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : إن جعلت طه تعديدا لأسماء الحروف فهذا ابتداء كلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p4/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p4/r7.claim: A variant reading has ما نزل عليك القرءان instead of ما أنزلنا عليك القرءان.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4/r7.anchor: قرىء { ما نزل * عليك القرءان لتشقى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r1.claim: Muqātil reports that Abū Jahl, al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, Muṭʿim b. ʿAdī, and al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith said Muhammad suffered for abandoning his fathers' religion; after his answer that he was sent as mercy, they repeated the taunt and the verse rebutted them.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل إن أبا جهل والوليد بن المغيرة ومطعم بن عدي والنضر بن الحارث قالوا لرسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r2.claim: Another reported occasion is that the Prophet prayed at night until his feet swelled, and Gabriel told him to spare himself because his body had a right over him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r2.anchor: أنه عليه السلام صلى بالليل حتى تورمت قدماه فقال له جبريل عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r3.claim: The same explanation includes a report that the Prophet tied his chest with a rope at night to keep from sleeping; some say he stood on one foot or stayed awake all night.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r3.anchor: وروى أيضا أنه عليه السلام : ( كان إذا قام من الليل ربط صدره بحبل حتى لا ينام )

RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī rejects the worship-based explanation as unlikely: if the Prophet did these things, they were commanded by God, so they would be happiness rather than something God says He had not commanded.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r4.anchor: قال القاضي هذا بعيد لأنه عليه السلام إن فعل شيئا من ذلك فلا بد وأن يكون قد فعله بأمر الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r5.claim: Another reading of the address is: do not distress yourself grieving over their disbelief; the Qur'an was sent as a reminder, and each person's belief or unbelief concerns that person, while Muhammad must only deliver.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون المراد لا تشق على نفسك ولا تعذبها بالأسف على كفر هؤلاء فإنا إنما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتذكر به

RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r6.claim: A further interpretation is that Muhammad is not blamed or held accountable for his people's disbelief once he has conveyed the message.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r6.anchor: ورابعها : أنك لا تلام على كفر قومك كقوله تعالى : { لست عليهم }

RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r7.claim: Because this was among the earliest Meccan sūras, when the Prophet was overpowered by enemies, the verse promises that he would not remain humiliated and would rise to honor.
RAZI-FULL:v22p4#2/r7.anchor: أن هذه السورة من أوائل ما نزل بمكة وفي ذلك الوقت كان عليه السلام مقهورا تحت ذل أعدائه

QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r9.claim: The Quran’s purpose is not to impose worship as hardship; it opens connection and prepares the ground of nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r9.anchor: أي ليس المقصود من إيجابنا إليك تعبدك ، وإنما هذا استفتاح الوصلة

QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r10.claim: After the Prophet was told not to covet worldly goods given to others (15:88), he stood in abstinence and worship; the response questions his great toil.
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r10.anchor: ويقال إنه لما قال له : { ولا تمدن عينيك إلى ما متعنا به أزواجا منهم }

QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r11.speaker: النبي
QUSHAYRI:v2p252/r11.claim: The Prophet explained his worship by asking, ‘Should I not be a grateful servant?’

STUDYQURAN:20:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r1.claim: The Quran was not sent to distress the Prophet over whether his people accept or reject it or believe his message.
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r1.anchor: The Quran was not given to the Prophet to cause him to be distressed over its acceptance or rejection by his people

STUDYQURAN:20:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r2.claim: The verse belongs to the wider theme of God addressing prophets' human reactions to rejection and trial.
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r2.anchor: this verse relates to the wider Quranic theme of God’s addressing the prophets’ human reactions to the trials they encountered

STUDYQURAN:20:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r3.speaker: another interpretation
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r3.claim: Another interpretation says the Prophet prayed all night until his legs swelled, and the verse told him not to exhaust himself in worship.
STUDYQURAN:20:2/r3.anchor: the Prophet had been praying all night to the point that his legs had become swollen

TAB-FULL:v16p7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p7/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p7/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people had remarked that the man had suffered for his Lord, so God revealed that the Quran was not sent down to make him suffer.
TAB-FULL:v16p7/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {طه ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى} [طه: 2] فإن قومه قالوا: لقد شقي هذا الرجل بربه

TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r4.claim: Addressing a man, God did not send down the Quran to burden Muhammad with work beyond his capacity.
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r4.anchor: ما أنزلناه عليك فنكلفك ما لا طاقة لك به من العمل

TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r5.claim: Mujahid relates the verse to 73:20: worshippers would hang ropes from their chests during prayer, and the Quran was not sent to make the Prophet suffer.
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، {ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى} [طه: 2] قال: هي مثل قوله: {فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه}

TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r6.claim: Qatadah says God did not make Muhammad wretched; He made him a mercy, a light, and a guide to Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى} [طه: 2] لا والله ما جعله الله شقيا، ولكن جعله رحمة ونورا، ودليلا إلى الجنة

TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r7.speaker: ذكر
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r7.claim: A report says this was said because of the toil, hardship, and long night vigils Muhammad endured.
TAB-FULL:v16p7#2/r7.anchor: وذكر أنه قيل له ذلك بسبب ما كان يلقى من النصب والعناء والسهر في قيام الليل

SULAMI:v1p434#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p434#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p434#2/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti derives the name Qur'an from its being conjoined with its speaker and not separate from Him, like sunlight and heat reaching us without separating from the sun's disk.
SULAMI:v1p434#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : سمي القرآن قرآنا لأنه مقارن

SULAMI:v1p434#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p434#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p434#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ata reads the verse as saying the Prophet should not suffer in God's service: his extra worship is gratitude for the nearness, communion, and service God granted him, and the gnostics find repose in such service.
SULAMI:v1p434#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : في قوله : ﴿ ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن

SULAMI:v1p434#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p434#2/r3.speaker: النبي
SULAMI:v1p434#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ata cites the Prophet's reply to being asked why he worshipped so intensely after forgiveness: he asked whether he should not be a grateful servant.

TABRISI:20:1-2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:1-2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:1-2/r6.claim: Shaqāʾ is continuing hardship for the soul, the opposite of felicity.
TABRISI:20:1-2/r6.anchor: الشقاء استمرار ما يشق على النفس ونقيضه السعادة

TABRISI:20:1-2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:1-2/r10.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:20:1-2/r10.claim: On this reading Ṭā Hā means “tread the ground with both feet.”

TABRISI:20:1-2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:1-2/r11.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:20:1-2/r11.claim: A report says the Prophet raised one foot while praying to increase exertion; after this verse was revealed, he lowered it.
TABRISI:20:1-2/r11.anchor: فأنزل الله { طه ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى } فوضعها

TABRISI:20:1-2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:1-2/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:20:1-2/r12.claim: The same account of the Prophet's exertion in prayer and the verse's response is also reported from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
TABRISI:20:1-2/r12.anchor: وروي ذلك عن أبي عبد الله ع

TABRISI:20:1-2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:1-2/r14.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:20:1-2/r14.claim: Al-Zajjāj also allows Ṭā Hā to function like an oath, making the verse its response.
TABRISI:20:1-2/r14.anchor: فيكون { ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى } جواب القسم

THALABI:v6p235#3/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p235#3/r13.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
THALABI:v6p235#3/r13.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī says God swore by His stature and guidance; the oath's answer is that He did not send the Qurʾān to make the Prophet suffer.
THALABI:v6p235#3/r13.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي: أقسم الله تعالى بطوله وهدايته، وموضع القاسم قوله ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r1.claim: Toil means becoming exhausted and reaching the limit of strenuous effort.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r1.anchor: أي: لتتعب وتبلغ من الجهد ما بلغت.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq explains the toil as praying on one leg, which makes the worship arduous.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أي لتصلي على إحدى رجليك فيشتد عليك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says that after revelation began in Mecca, the Prophet intensified worship; God told him not to exhaust himself, and afterward he slept part of the night and prayed part.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r3.anchor: قال الكلبي: (لما نزل على رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- الوحي بمكة اجتهد في العبادة واشتدت عبادته،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r4.claim: Muqatil gives another occasion: Abu Jahl and the polytheists said the Prophet was suffering by abandoning worldly life, so the verse answered them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p351#3/r4.anchor: وذكر مقاتل في سبب النزول غير هذا وهو أنه قال: (قال أبو جهل # والمشركون للنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r4.claim: The address again means “O man”; God did not send down the Quran to make the Prophet suffer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r4.anchor: يقول: يا رجل {ما أنزلنا عليك القرءان لتشقى} [طه: 2] .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r5.claim: Mujahid takes the toil to be excessive prayer, connecting the verse with the instruction to recite what is easy in 73:20; people tied ropes to their chests while praying.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r5.anchor: أخبرني عاصم بن حكيم أن مجاهدا قال: لتشقى في الصلاة كقوله: {فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه} [المزمل: 20]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r6.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet saw a rope between two mosque pillars, learned it helped a woman stay upright during prayer, and told her to pray while alert and sleep when overcome.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r6.anchor: عن حميد الطويل، عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رأى حبلا ممدودا بين ساريتين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r7.claim: The Prophet said to pray at night only as long as one understands the prayer, and to sleep when the Quran becomes difficult to recite.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r7.anchor: قال رسول الله: «ليصل أحدكم من الليل ما عقل صلاته، فإذا استعجم عليه القرآن فلينم»

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r8.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the polytheists called the Prophet wretched, and God revealed this verse in response.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p251/r8.anchor: وكان الحسن يقول: إن المشركين قالوا للنبي إنه شقي، فأنزل الله تبارك وتعالى هذه الآية

ELMALILI:v1p119/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p119/r1.speaker: Üseyd b. Hudayr
ELMALILI:v1p119/r1.claim: Elmalılı says Bukhari reports that while Usayd b. Hudayr recited Sūrat al-Baqara, angels descended successively in the darkness to the sound of his recitation.
ELMALILI:v1p119/r1.anchor: Buhârî’de de Üseyd b. Hudayr radıyallahu ‘anh Hazretleri’nin[^3] Sûre-i Bakara okumasıyla sesine karanlıkta peyderpey melâike inmiş olduğu

ELMALILI:v1p119/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p119/r2.speaker: Ukbe b. Âmir
ELMALILI:v1p119/r2.claim: Ukba ibn Amir reports that at the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet exhorted them to hold fast to the Qur’an.
ELMALILI:v1p119/r2.anchor: Ukbe[^6] b. Âmir radıyallahu ‘anh demiştir ki: “Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Haccetü’l-vedâ‘da bize[^7] ahd verdi de buyurdu ki: (عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْقُرْآنِ)

ELMALILI:v1p119/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p119/r3.speaker: Resûl-i Ekrem
ELMALILI:v1p119/r3.claim: Asked which reciter was best in recitation or voice, the Prophet said it was the one whose fear of God is evident when heard.
ELMALILI:v1p119/r3.anchor: Bir de Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi

ELMALILI:v1p119/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p119/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p119/r4.claim: These reports clarify that reading Qur’an and tafsir aims at reminding those who fear God: the Qur’an was not sent to impose hardship, but as a reminder for the God-fearing.
ELMALILI:v1p119/r4.anchor: Bununla Kur’an ve tefsir okumaktan maksad ne olduğunu da anlamış oluyoruz.

ELMALILI:v1p119/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p119/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p119/r5.claim: Elmalılı prays that God illuminate their hearts with the light of the Qur’an.
ELMALILI:v1p119/r5.anchor: Heman Cenâb-ı Allah kalblerimizi nûr-i Kur’an ile tenvîr buyursun.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r1.claim: The phrase can mean “so that you become unhappy” or “so that you suffer hardship and toil.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r1.anchor: “mutsuz olasın diye indirmedik” şeklinde çevirdiğimiz kısmını “eziyet, zahmet çekesin diye indirmedik”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s message is not meant to extinguish the joy of life; it guides, reminds, and warns those who accept their human responsibility and fear failing it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r2.anchor: yaratılış amacına uygun bir sorumluluk bilinci taşıyanlara yol göstermek, hatırlatma ve uyarılarda bulunmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r3.speaker: bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r3.claim: Some exegetes, linking reports of the Prophet’s preaching hardships and exhaustion from night worship, read the verse as saying the Qur’an does not impose beyond one’s capacity; worship is not intended as hardship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r3.anchor: Bazı müfessirler Resûlullah’ın tebliğ görevi esnasında çektiği sıkıntıları ve gece ibadetinden ötürü tâkatten düştüğünü anlatan rivayetlerle bağ kurarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r4.speaker: bazıları
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r4.claim: Other commentators take the verse as glad tidings that the Prophet would not remain in hardship but would attain strength, prestige, and recognition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r4.anchor: bazıları da burada, Hz. Peygamber’in hep bu sıkıntılı duruma mahkûm kalmayıp güçlü ve itibarlı olacağı ve değerinin bilineceği günlere de kavuşacağı yönünde müjde verildiği yorumunu yapmışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r5.claim: In context, the passage consoles a demoralized Prophet and implies he should not ruin himself over people who resist truth and worship handmade idols; the reminder benefits those conscious of responsibility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:2/r5.anchor: mâneviyat kırıklığına uğrayan Hz. Peygamber’e teselli verildiği, Kur’an’ın, ancak insan olmanın sorumluluğunu taşıyanlar

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when revelation first came, the Prophet stood on his toes while praying; this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أول ما أنزل الله عليه الوحي يقوم على صدور قدميه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ b. Anas reports that the Prophet shifted his weight between his feet while standing in prayer, until this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r2.anchor: واخرج عبد الله بن حميد في تفسيره عن الربيع بن أنس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يراوح بين قدميه ليقوم على كل رجل

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that people said the man had become wretched because of his Lord, and this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن مردويه من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس قال قالوا لقد شقي هذا الرجل بربه فأنزل الله

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p303/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p303/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p303/r1.claim: Muqatil says Abu Jahl and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith called Muhammad wretched for leaving their religion, referring to his long worship and strenuous devotion; the verse answered them.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p303/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: قال أبو جهل، والنضر بن الحارث للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p303/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p303/r2.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p303/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that when Muhammad and his companions stood to pray after the Quran came down, Quraysh said it had been revealed only to make him suffer; the verse was revealed in response.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p303/r2.anchor: عن جويبر، عن الضحاك قال: لما نزل القرآن على النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قام هو وأصحابه فصلوا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r5.claim: The first Qurʾanic sense of shaqāʾ is toil, including the statements that the Prophet was not burdened with the Qurʾan and the follower will not suffer.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p370#2/r5.anchor: أحدها : التعب . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في سورة طه )

BURHAN:v4p237/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p237/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p237/r8.claim: Here “except” means “rather,” so the verse says the Qur'an was sent as a reminder, not to cause distress.
BURHAN:v4p237/r8.anchor: الثاني بمعنى بل كقوله تعالى ﴿ طه ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى إلا تذكرة ﴾ 2 أي بل تذكرة

RUMMANI:v1p97/r8.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p97/r8.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p97/r8.claim: He exemplifies identical ending letters with the linked endings in the opening of Ṭā Hā and the opening of al-Ṭūr.
RUMMANI:v1p97/r8.anchor: فالحروف المتجانسة كقوله تعالى: {طه ما أنزلنا عليك القرآن لتشقى إلا تذكرة لمن يخشى}. الآيات. وكقوله: {والطور وكتاب مسطور}

DAMGHANI:v1p266/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r13.claim: Shaqāʾ can mean fatigue or toil, as in the statement that the Qur'an was not sent to make the Prophet weary.
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r13.anchor: الثالث : الشقاء التعب قوله تعالى في سورة طه
